newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Libya invites Arab immigrants in Kuwait advert.
newsitem.headline: Libya invites Arab immigrants in Kuwait advert.

text.p: Libya on Sunday invited "productive" Arabs to emigrate to the north African Arab state, promising work, ownership and travel rights and permanent residency status.
A Libyan statement published in advertisement form in Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam newspaper said Libya needed immigrants "to take part in building the ideal Arab society on the land of all Arabs (Libya)".

Libya's economy is stagnant partly due to sanctions imposed by the United Nations against the oil-rich state since 1992 over suspected Libyan involvement in the bombing of a Pan Am flight over Scotland in 1988 which killed 270 people.

A Libyan diplomatic mission official declined comment on the statement, which he said was published by the mission in Kuwait upon instruction from Libya's equivalent of a foreign ministry for Arab world affairs.
The advertisement said Arab citizens who went to work in Libya would "enjoy full Arab citizenship rights".

Hundreds of Arab Palestinians have been stranded at a desert camp on libya's border with Egypt since September 1995, when Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi ejected thousands of Palestinians to show the futility of their leader's peace pacts with Israel.
Many Palestinians have since returned to the Palestinian self-rule areas but those without papers required to enter Egypt or the Gaza Strip and the West Bank remain stranded.
An Arab who called the mission to investigate the requirements said he was told to apply and wait for an answer from Tripoli.
